notes: Four bullets, two steps. Bullets 1 and 2 are not a journey -- they are how you REACH Vilatroire: he stands in a walled watchtower in West Ronfaure that can only be entered through the zone line at (C-7) in Northern San d'Oria, so a player already standing in West Ronfaure cannot walk to him. That is route information about step 1's own target, not a rung of its own, and a 'travel to West Ronfaure' step would be an unmarkable duplicate of the zone step 1 already carries. Bullet 4's real content is the party condition: two members, both the same race as each other. Nothing in the packets reports party composition or race, so it is a note on the final talk rather than a step -- a rung the player cannot be tracked through. 'Quest Reqs: Level 10 and up' is the level gate; no job is named, so jobs stays empty.

notes: The door is the problem. The page names the same entity two different ways -- 'Door: House to the West of Collet' in bullet 2 and 'Door: House West of Collet' in bullet 4 -- and NEITHER reads like a client entity name: every real door already in the index is abbreviated to fit the client's field ('Door: Prince Royal's Rm', 'Door: Svenja's Rm', 'Door: Research Chamber'). These are wiki descriptions of a door's position, not its name. The shorter bullet-4 form is recorded because it is the one attached to the completing step, the longer form is kept here, and the quest stays at medium: the ladder is certainly right, but steps 2 and 4 will probably fail to bind to a live entity and lose their markers. Worth a qmprobe dump of Upper Jeuno to settle. VERIFY PASS: the draft made bullet 3 an observable rung with the [KI] Clock tower oil as its evidence. That breaks the rule that evidence must be obtained AT the step -- the oil is obtained by finishing Deal with Tenshodo, a different quest, and the header lists it under Item Reqs, which means the ordinary player already holds it when this quest is accepted. Its evidence would have fired immediately and jumped the mark to the final door, skipping two cutscenes the quest genuinely requires. Bullet 3 is a cross-quest precondition, not a ladder position: evidence nulled, the rung marked optional and demoted, and the oil kept where it is actually used -- as the items requirement on step 4. Nothing observable now remains in this quest, which is the honest result. Reward is gil and Engineer's Gloves, so no reward is being used as evidence anywhere.

bullet 3 states a requirement, it does not give an instruction: the [KI] Clock tower oil is granted by the separate quest Deal with Tenshodo and is listed in the header under Item Reqs, so a player will normally already be holding it before this quest is even accepted. Holding it therefore proves nothing about a position in THIS ladder. Evidence removed and the rung marked optional -- as evidence it would have satisfied step 3 at accept time and thrown the marker forward to the final door check, skipping the Collet cutscene and the first door cutscene that the quest really does require.

Item Reqs renders as 'Revival Root Revival Tree Root', which is one wiki link and its display text; both spellings resolve to item 940 and the long form is recorded, per the guide. notes: The cleanest page in the batch: three bullets, three steps, a key item handed over at each of the first two so the ladder is fully observable end to end. Both harpoons are key items and both are named in full on the page, so evidence is real rather than reached for -- holding the Broken harpoon draws Shipilolo, holding the Extravagant harpoon draws Jorin. The Broken harpoon is carried as a requirement on step 2 as well as being step 1's evidence, which is not the duplicate-evidence hazard: it is evidence exactly once. Both NPCs are in Western Adoulin -- (J-4) at the Waterfront and (J-9) outside the Inventors' Coalition -- so no step spans a zone. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only FLevel 1 and the raw string survive.

notes: Bullet 2's four NPCs are one bullet holding four visits with no order stated anywhere on the page, so they share a group and all four draw at once. A strict ladder would mark Purere alone and leave the other three dark until you happened to walk past them, which is exactly the failure the group mechanism exists for. All five NPCs are inside Abyssea - Uleguerand, so the group members each keep the same zone. The page locates them by Conflux number rather than by grid -- only Conflux #7 is given a grid, (F-7) -- so Purere inherits (F-7) because the page says she is at the same Conflux as Tyamah, and the other three carry no grid rather than a fabricated one. The wiki '(A)' suffix is kept on every name because the guide says to write the wiki form and let the normaliser fold it; it does, all four fold to the plain in-game name. Fame 'aule' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only the raw string and FLevel 2 survive.

notes: Bullets 2 and 3 are one step, not two: 'travel to West Ronfaure to locate a ???' and 'touch it' are the same act of finding and clicking one object, and a separate travel rung would be an unmarkable duplicate of the zone the examine step already carries. The ??? spawns in ONE of three places -- the G-10/G-11 border, (G-9) at the outpost, or (F-11) by the wall in the south of the square -- and which one is not knowable ahead of time, so the grid is deliberately null and all three are written into the note. Picking one would point the player at the wrong corner of the zone two times in three. The ??? resolves as an object with no key, so it keeps its rung and carries no marker, which is the expected outcome for every ??? in the corpus. The step is still worth having: it holds the Gulemont's document key item, which is what makes the return trip to Gulemont readable.

notes: This is the subjob quest, so getting it wrong is expensive. Bullet 2 is three trades, not one: the page says the Wild Rabbit Tail 'then' the Dhalmel Saliva 'and finally' the Bloody Robe, which is an explicit order, and they are not held as a set -- you can hand them over one at a time. Three ordered steps on the same NPC is one marker that keeps asking for the next thing, and it means holding only the rabbit tail already reads as ready. Folding them into a single AND-list of three would demand all three at once, which the page never says. The trailing NOTE paragraph is not a step but it IS quest content, and the header backs it: [KI] Gilgamesh's introductory letter, from the Rhapsodies of Vana'diel mission Set Free, 'replaces the need for the requested items'. That is a genuine second way to satisfy the same steps, so the letter is carried in items_alt on all three trades. Demoted to medium for one honest reason: the page never says what you DO with the letter -- show it, trade it, or simply talk -- so the branch's shape is modelled from the header's OR and not from an instruction. 'Quest Reqs: Level 18' is the level gate, any job. The reward is a Support Job, which is not an item and cannot be evidence of anything.

notes: One top-level bullet, split into two steps because its sub-bullet moves you to another zone and the schema is one step, one zone: the Imp Wings come off Orderly Imps in Caedarva Mire (Map 1), and the trade happens in Aht Urhgan Whitegate. The obtain step is what makes the zone and the mob markable at all; folded into the trade step, Caedarva Mire would have vanished from the record entirely. Holding an Imp Wing is real evidence -- it is a normal item, not the reward, which is the PFC Wildcat badge. The auction house is the other source (Materials > Alchemy 1) and needs no marker. The header writes the start grid as '(1-10)', which is not a legal grid reference: columns are letters, and this is the familiar I-to-1 transcription slip, so (I-10) is recorded and the header string is preserved verbatim in start.raw. The real gate is 'Complete 25 points worth of Assaults as Private Second Class' -- a mercenary rank plus an Assault point total, neither of which has a slot in the schema nor any observable predicate, so it is flagged and gates nothing. It is not a level gate and not a job gate; jobs stays empty.
